entities.name: Azerbaijan State Museum of History of Religion
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Azerbaijan State Museum of History of Religion (Azerbaijani: Azərbaycan Dövlət Din Tarixi Muzeyi) in Baku, Azerbaijan, preserves and presents materials documenting the extraordinary religious diversity and historical evolution of religious practice in Azerbaijan — a country at the crossroads of ancient Zoroastrianism (the Ateshgah fire temple and Azerbaijan's reputation as the 'Land of Fire'), early Christianity (Caucasian Albanian Christianity), Islam (the dominant religion since the 7th-8th centuries CE), and Soviet state atheism that suppressed all religious practice for 70 years.

Azerbaijan's religious history is exceptionally rich: the Baku area's natural gas vents (eternal flames) made it a sacred site of Zoroastrian fire worship from ancient times; the Ateshgah Fire Temple near Baku was used by Hindu Sikh and Zoroastrian pilgrims well into the 19th century. Caucasian Albania (the ancient Christian kingdom of what is now Azerbaijan, 1st-8th centuries CE) had its own autocephalous church tradition before being Islamicized. The country then received Shi'a Islam through Safavid Persian influence in the 16th century, making Azerbaijan (along with Iran) one of the world's predominantly Shi'a-Muslim countries.

The museum's collection spans Zoroastrian fire worship artifacts, Caucasian Albanian Christian materials, Islamic art and documents, Jewish (Mountain Jews) heritage, and materials from the Soviet atheist period. This comprehensive scope makes it one of the world's most unusual religion museums — covering the full evolutionary arc of spiritual practice in a single territory.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Azerbaijan State Museum of History of Religion — covering the full arc from ancient Zoroastrian fire worship through Caucasian Albanian Christianity to Shi'a Islam, documenting one of the world's most religiously diverse historical territories — is historically significant as a monument to Azerbaijan's extraordinary religious heritage spanning millennia.
